//: What a release needs built after it lands. Read from the NEW checkout, which is the point: the update script that runs during an update is the one being replaced, so a release cannot teach an older shell anything through code. It can through data — an older shell reads this file from what it just pulled, so a release that adds a whole new directory works on shells that shipped before that directory existed.

migrations.name: standalone
migrations.label: hand the session from Quickshell to cae
migrations.says: cae draws the whole desktop now, so the session no longer needs Quickshell to start it or to carry its keys. This installs cae-shell.service, stops execs.lua starting Quickshell, and repoints the caelestia:* keybinds at cae's door. A copy of each file it edits is kept beside it, and `cae-shell/standalone.py --undo` puts everything back.
migrations.after: the session starts cae at the next login; `cae restart` wakes it now

//migrations: Changes to the machine that a release needs and a build cannot make: a unit to enable, a config line to retire. Read from the NEW checkout for the same reason `components` is. `done` is a test that must be true when there is nothing left to do — it is run before and after, so a migration that half-applied on a previous run is finished rather than repeated. `run` is the whole of it, and must be safe to run twice.
